title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 6–12). C_0 is the 'isotopic' category of oriented anabelian surfaces of finite type, i.e. hyperbolic surfaces. Its morphisms are isotopy classes of finite coverings, and its isomorphisms are mapping classes. Ĉ_0 is its 'profinite compactification', whose Hom-sets are the completed sets Hom^ of (12). On this page Grothendieck describes the morphisms of Ĉ_0 and shows that composition in Ĉ_0 is well defined and computable.

(1) Factorization, (18)–(19). Every Ĉ_0-morphism f̂ : X → Y factors as X —f̂_0→ Y' —u→ Y. Here u is a genuine C_0-morphism (a finite covering) and f̂_0 is a Ĉ_0-isomorphism. Because Ĉ_0 → C_0 is conservative on objects, Y' is in fact C_0-isomorphic to X.
- Left marginal NB: Isom_{Ĉ_0}(X,Y) ≅ Isom_{C_0}(X,Y)^, a torsor under Aut_{Ĉ_0}(X) ≅ Aut_{C_0}(X)^, the profinite completion of the mapping class group.
- Uniqueness: suppose that for every covering u : Y' → Y the composite Aut_Y(Y') → Aut(Y') → Aut(Y')^ is injective. Then the pair (Y', u) is determined by f̂ up to unique Y-isomorphism. Here Aut_Y(Y') is the finite deck group. Injectivity holds because a nontrivial deck transformation of a hyperbolic surface is not isotopic to the identity, and mapping class groups are residually finite (Grossman 1974).

(2) Composition, (20)–(22). Take f̂ = u f̂_0 and ĝ = v ĝ_0 with ĝ_0 : Y ≅ Z' and v : Z' → Z. To compose, ĝ_0 must be moved past u.
- Let H_u ⊂ Aut(Y) be the mapping classes of Y that lift along u.
- Let G_u ⊂ Aut(Y') × Aut(Y) be the pairs (φ', φ) with φu = uφ'. Then G_u → H_u is surjective with finite kernel Aut_Y(Y').
- H_u has finite index in Aut(Y), since Aut(Y) permutes the finitely many index-n subgroups of π_1. Hence its closure Ĥ_u is open in Aut(Y)^.
- Since Isom_{C_0}(Y,Z') is dense in the Aut(Y)^-torsor Isom^, one can write ĝ_0 = wφ̂, with w : Y ≅ Z' a genuine C_0-isomorphism and φ̂ ∈ Ĥ_u.
- The lifting homomorphism extends to completions, Ĝ_u → Ĥ_u, so there is φ̂' ∈ Aut(Y')^ with φ̂u = uφ̂'.
- Hence ĝf̂ = (vwu)(φ̂' f̂_0). This is again a C_0-morphism after a Ĉ_0-isomorphism, i.e. of the normal form (19).

Purpose. This gives an explicit 'covering ∘ completed-isotopy' calculus for the profinite isotopic category. The next page reinterprets the completed isomorphisms as étale paths (pro-morphisms) in the fundamental groupoid of the moduli stack. It also observes that the construction works over any algebraically closed field k, functorially in k, which is the route to a Galois action on the 'Teichmüller' category.
errors: (18) is written f̂ : X̂ → Y. The hat on X is a slip or emphasis; the morphism is X → Y in Ĉ_0.

The uniqueness claim relies on the injectivity hypothesis on Aut_Y(Y') → Aut(Y')^. This is true for hyperbolic surfaces, but only because mapping class groups are residually finite (Grossman) and deck transformations are non-isotopic to the identity. These facts are not stated on the page.

Two points are left implicit. First, Ĝ_u → Ĥ_u is surjective; this holds because any homomorphism between discrete groups is continuous for the profinite topologies. Second, the composite (φ̂', f̂_0) does not depend on the choice of the approximation w. The latter is presumably handled by the uniqueness of (19). No genuine error appears.

The page never needs the congruence-type question of whether the topology induced on G_u from Aut(Y')^ equals its full profinite topology. That is correct for the composition argument, but the issue resurfaces for faithfulness and comparison with the étale fundamental groupoid, and it is not discussed here.

ideas.what: Profinite completion of the isotopic (mapping-class + finite covering) category of hyperbolic surfaces, with morphisms factored as finite covering ∘ completed mapping-class isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: profinite Teichmüller tower / profinite mapping class groupoid enriched with finite étale covers; cf. procongruence/profinite Teichmüller theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Teichmüller tower) for the groupoid; profinite versions developed by Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) treats the Teichmüller tower of mapping class groupoids, but without this explicit covering+completion category and its factorization calculus

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the factorization via injectivity of the deck group Aut_Y(Y') into the completed mapping class group of Y'
ideas.modern_name: residual finiteness of mapping class groups; faithfulness of finite group actions on Mod^

ideas.what: Commuting a completed isomorphism past a covering using the finite-index liftable subgroup H_u and the correspondence G_u ⊂ Aut(Y')×Aut(Y)
ideas.modern_name: liftable mapping class groups / Birman–Hilden-type correspondence, completed profinitely
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman–Hilden (lifting theory); profinite version folklore in anabelian/GT literature

missed.claim: This is an explicit calculus for a profinite category whose objects are hyperbolic surfaces. Its morphisms are finite coverings composed with completed mapping-class isomorphisms, and composition is computed by approximating with genuine isomorphisms and lifting through open subgroups. Grothendieck intended it as the object on which Gal(Q̄/Q) acts. The published Esquisse speaks only of the Teichmüller groupoid of isomorphisms, not of this mixed category including coverings.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates a Galois action on a 'Teichmüller category with coverings', compatible with passage to finite covers. This is close to what Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki and work on GT and covers study piecemeal. The categorical packaging is modest, but it documents Grothendieck's early (c. 1978–81) formulation.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is routine given residual finiteness and lifting of mapping classes. Of mild interest is the explicit categorical formulation of a profinite isotopic category including finite coverings, intended to carry a Galois action. That is a slightly richer object than the Teichmüller groupoid of the Esquisse, but not a surprising or unknown result.

'on voit que Y' est déterminé par f̂ à Y-isom. unique près' — the following lines concern morphismes finis 'réalisés'; 'plus, partout' is struck out.

'(20)' line: 'et le mettre sous la même forme ...; on approche ĝ_0 (Ĉ_0-iso.) par ...'. The left marginal note includes 'Isom_{Ĉ_0}(X,Y) ≃ Isom_{C_0}(X,Y)^ et Aut_{Ĉ_0}(X) ≃ Aut_{C_0}(X)^' and refers to the functor Ĉ_0 → C_0 being conservative.
The centre marginal note reads roughly: 'NB Il faut savoir ... ĝ_0 = wφ̂ ... signifie (φ̂',φ̂) ∈ Ĝ_u, G_u ⊂ Aut(Y')×Aut(Y), ... Ĥ_u image de Ĝ_u'.
